title: Pilot sprint decomposition and resource burn walkthrough
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working walkthrough for decomposing a 6-week POC into digestible sprints and tracking resource burn (FTE-hours) for both Solutions Engineering and Customer-side contributors. It combines the workshop agenda notes, sprint-by-sprint milestones, an action-oriented task tracker, acceptance criteria, and a lightweight risk map.

Context / problem statement:
Customer: fintech-midmarket (obfuscated). They need a secure, low-latency inference pipeline for document summarization and entity redaction. Goal: validate integration with Redwood Private (VPC) and demonstrate steady-state cost/latency under representative traffic (10 rps steady, spikes to 60 rps) and quantization profile. Timebox: 6 calendar weeks (including onboarding workshop and 2-week hypercare).

High-level success criteria (must pass):
- End-to-end demo: app -> Redwood Private endpoint -> summaries/redactions with PII masking, run in customer's VPC
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 450ms for 512-token prompt under normal load
- Cost: per-token inference cost projection with quantized model <= target threshold (customer budget)
- Security: KMS integration for key rotation, audit log delivery to customer SIEM
- Observability: traces and token-level cost view available in Redwood Console for the demo routes

Scope (what's in scope this POC):
- Model: 13B open model provided by customer, quantized to 4-bit using recommended pipeline
- Runtime: Redwood Private deployed into customer's AWS account (single AZ) with a dedicated pool of 4 GPUs for peak testing
- Integrations: customer S3 ingress/egress, KMS for key management, and customer CI to exercise integration tests
- Evals: 200-sample prompt set for quality/regression detection

Out of scope:
- Multi-region HA, full production capacity planning, and long-term cost optimization program

Workshop runbook (Onboarding + Alignment - Day 0):
- 09:00 - 09:15: Introductions & goals (SE lead: Maya).
- 09:15 - 09:45: Architecture review (customer infra owner + Redwood infra).
- 09:45 - 10:30: Data flow tabletop (S3->preproc->inference->postproc->S3). Identify preproc constraints and privacy controls.
- 10:30 - 11:00: Acceptance criteria and success matrix review (captured here).
- 11:00 - 11:30: Quick walk-through of Redwood Console (observability hooks, rollouts) - demo account.
- 11:30 - 12:00: Immediate blockers & action items (assign owners).

Sprint decomposition (6-week calendar view):
Week 0 (prework, 5 days before workshop):
- Tasks: Account provisioning, IAM roles & VPC peering prep, share SSH keys, baseline network tests (latency/bandwidth).
- Owners: Customer infra (network), SE infra (Evan).
- Estimated burn: 10 FTE-hours SE + 8 FTE-hours customer.

Week 1 (Onboarding + deploy Redwood Private):
- Tasks: Deploy control plane, bootstrap node pool (1 GPU), validate KMS connectivity, basic inference smoke tests with small model.
- Owners: SE infra (Evan, Luis), customer infra.
- Deliverables: Live endpoint, audit log path, demo script ready.
- Burn estimate: 40 FTE-hours SE, 20 customer.

Week 2 (Model quantization & workload integration):
- Tasks: Quantize 13B model (baseline q4), integrate model into runtime, run synthetic load tests (ramp to 30 rps), collect p95 numbers.
- Owners: Applied ML (Priya), SE infra (Luis).
- Deliverables: Quantized model artifact, perf report.
- Burn estimate: 60 FTE-hours SE+ML combined, 10 customer.

Week 3 (Feature integration + routing policies):
- Tasks: Implement request routing rules, prefix caching config, integrate preprocessing (PII redaction), run functional regression evals.
- Owners: Solutions Eng (Maya), Applied ML (Priya).
- Deliverables: Route configs, eval baseline.
- Burn estimate: 45 FTE-hours SE, 12 customer.

Week 4 (Scale testing & cost modeling):
- Tasks: Load test to 60 rps, exercise autoscaling/burst capacity, measure cost per 10k tokens for observed patterns, iterate quantization if quality drops.
- Owners: SE infra, Observability (Evan), Product (consult).
- Deliverables: Scale test report, cost model spreadsheet.
- Burn estimate: 55 FTE-hours SE, 6 customer.

Week 5 (Demo hardening + runbook):
- Tasks: Create final demo script, create rollback/fallback policy (model variant fallback), finalize acceptance checklist, customer sign-off rehearsal.
- Owners: Solutions Eng (Maya), Customer PM.
- Deliverables: Demo runbook, rollback playbook.
- Burn estimate: 30 FTE-hours SE, 8 customer.

Week 6 (Hypercare 2-week window overlapping):
- Tasks: 2-weeks of monitored live traffic (small traffic), triage meetings twice weekly, fix any regressions; capture post-POC recommendations.
- Burn estimate: 20 FTE-hours/week SE (ongoing), customer on-call participation.

Aggregate resource burn (rough):
- Solutions Eng (SE leads, infra, applied ML): ~260 FTE-hours across 6 weeks
- Customer: ~64 FTE-hours scheduled
- Notes: This is a working estimate; track actuals in the spreadsheet (linked artifact).

Task tracker (actionable items captured during workshop):
- ACTION-001: Create customer onboarding IAM doc + minimal policies (owner: Evan) - due: 2025-11-07 - status: blocked (waiting for customer VPC info).
- ACTION-002: Quantization run for 13B: baseline q4 -> artifacts to S3 (owner: Priya) - due: 2025-11-14 - status: in_progress.
- ACTION-003: Draft demo script with edge-case prompts (owner: Maya) - due: 2025-11-18 - status: in_progress.
- ACTION-004: Configure Console traces for demo routes + add webhook to Slack channel (owner: Luis) - due: 2025-11-10 - status: todo.
- ACTION-005: Customer to share sample dataset (PII-scrubbed) for evals (owner: Customer Data Owner) - due: 2025-11-09 - status: pending.

Acceptance checklist (pass/fail gates):
- End-to-end request path validated with sample dataset (pass: yes/no).
- p95 latency recorded under steady load and spike tests.
- KMS integration verified (rotate-key test passed).
- Audit logs delivered to customer SIEM for at least 24 hours of traffic.
- Quality regression < 5% delta vs baseline on sensitive prompts.

Mini risk register (working):
- Risk: Quantization degrades quality significantly (>10% drift). Mitigation: Keep a float model fallback and run A/B evals; schedule extra ML tuning week if needed.
- Risk: Customer network egress limits cause cold-start spikes. Mitigation: Pre-warm nodes, advise customer on NAT gateway sizing.
- Risk: KMS policy prevents test rotations. Mitigation: Run policy review during Week 0 and schedule joint call with security.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Q: Do we have a standard template for the demo script that embeds token-level cost annotations? If not, add to infra-playbooks.
- Q: Should we include a tiny microbenchmark run on-customer with PyTorch kernels vs runtime? Decision: optional, only if perf gap appears.
- Note: customer asked about on-prem option; capture cost delta in final recommendations but out of scope for this POC.

Communication cadence (recommended):
- Stand-ups: Mon/Wed/Fri async updates in Slack channel (#pilot-fintech-poc).
- Syncs: Weekly 30-min sync with customer PM + technical leads (Tue 10am PT).
- Escalation: SE lead -> Head of SE -> On-call infra for outages.

Deliverables checklist to attach to final handoff:
- Final demo runbook (slides + script)
- Quantization artifacts + model card (quality metrics)
- Performance and cost report (per-route P95, token cost model)
- Audit log delivery proof and KMS test results
- Post-POC recommendations and production readiness scorecard

Next immediate steps (right after workshop):
1) Evan: confirm VPC peering details and open minimal IAM (due 2025-11-07).
2) Customer: upload 200-sample eval set (PII-scrubbed) to shared S3 (due 2025-11-09).
3) Priya: start quantization pipeline and post artifacts (due 2025-11-14).
4) Maya: update demo script with 5 edge-case prompts and circulate for review (due 2025-11-10).

Appendix A - quick links for SE team:
- Confluence onboarding checklist: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/POC+onboarding+checklist
- Template: demo-runbook-template (internal) - see linked repo PR #58
- Perf spreadsheet (internal): drive: /sheets/pilot-cost-model-2025-Q4

Informal notes (captured raw during call):
- "Customer mentioned weekly deploy freeze windows — need to confirm exact times" - Maya
- "If quantization needs extra tuning, call out as change request to customer for additional week" - Priya
- TODO: add an action to run a small privacy audit for the redaction pipeline; might need Legal review.

If you're reading this as the SE on-duty: update the Action tracker with status and hours spent after each major task; we'll reconcile burn vs estimate at the end of Week 3 and Week 6.

--- end of doc (working draft)
